Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Hill
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 75 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama Police Officers Standards and Training Commission (APOSTC) by an estimated $1.95 million dollars ($650,000 annually) over a 3-year period to provide all incumbent law enforcement officers crisis intervention training as a continuing education requirement.
This bill could also increase the financial obligations of the various law enforcement agencies for travel expenses and backfilling positions of those incumbent law enforcement officers required to receive this training in accordance with the provisions of this bill.
Allen Treadaway, Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security

Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 02/08/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 139 as introduced proposes a local Constitutional Amendment, which if ratified, would prohibit any municipality located entirely within Tuscaloosa County from increasing the rate of sales and use tax levied by the municipality, except by approval by a majority vote of the qualified electors of the municipality.
In addition, this bill will increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from the State General Fund, by an estimated $1,500 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023.
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs
